title: editor tutorial / Explore the user interface
content:
## Explore the user interface Take a quick tour of the user interface before you create the app. ### Switch between views with the Activity Bar 1. Use the Activity Bar to switch between views. ![Screenshot showing the Activity Bar.](../images/getting-started/activity-bar.png) > [!TIP] > Hover over an Activity Bar item to see its name and keyboard shortcut. Select the item again to close the view. 1. Notice that the **Primary Side Bar** changes to show information for the selected view. For example, the Run and Debug view contains controls for configuring and starting a debugging session. ![Screenshot showing the Activity Bar and the Run and Debug view in the Primary Side Bar.](../images/getting-started/activity-bar-and-side-bar.png) ### View and edit files with the Editor 1. Select the Explorer view in the Activity Bar, and then select **New File...**. ![Screenshot showing the New File button in the Explorer view.](../images/getting-started/explorer-new-file.png) 1. Enter `index.html`, and then press `kbstyle(Enter)`. The new file opens in an Editor in the main area of the window. ![Screenshot showing a new file open in the Editor.](../images/getting-started/new-file-editor.png) 1. Type `

My recipes

`. As you type, IntelliSense suggests ways to complete your code. Use `kbstyle(Up)` and `kbstyle(Down)` to navigate the suggestions, and use `kbstyle(Tab)` to insert a selected suggestion. 1. Save the file with `kb(workbench.action.files.save)`. 1. Select **New File...** again to create `style.css`, and then create `app.js`. Each file opens in a new Editor tab. You can open multiple editors and view them side by side. Learn more about [side-by-side editing](/docs/editing/getting-started/userinterface.md#side-by-side-editing). ![Screenshot showing multiple Editor tabs.](../images/getting-started/multiple-editors.png) ### Access the terminal from the Panel 1. Open the integrated terminal with `kb(workbench.action.terminal.toggleTerminal)`. You can also select **View** > **Terminal**. You can choose from the shells installed on your computer, such as PowerShell, Command Prompt, or Bash. ![Screenshot showing the Terminal in the Panel.](../images/getting-started/vscode-panel.png) 1. Enter the following command to create a file in the workspace. ```bash echo "Hello, VS Code" > greetings.txt ``` The terminal starts in the root of your workspace by default. Notice that the Explorer view automatically shows the new file. ![Screenshot showing the new file in the Explorer view.](../images/getting-started/terminal-new-file.png) 1. Select the **Launch Profile** dropdown to view the available shells and open another terminal. ![Screenshot showing the Launch Profile dropdown and available shells.](../images/getting-started/terminal-launch-profile.png) ### Access commands with the Command Palette 1. Open the Command Palette with `kb(workbench.action.showCommands)`. You can also select **View** > **Command Palette**. The Command Palette provides access to many {% data variables.product.prodname_vscode_shortname %} commands. Extensions can add more commands. ![Screenshot showing the Command Palette.](../images/getting-started/command-palette.png) 1. Try these Command Palette modes: * **Command mode (`>`)**: after the `>` symbol, type `move terminal` to find commands that move the terminal to a new window. ![Screenshot showing commands for moving the terminal in the Command Palette.](../images/getting-started/command-palette-move-terminal.png) * **Quick Open mode**: remove the `>` symbol, and then type a file name to search your workspace. Open Quick Open directly with `kb(workbench.action.quickOpen)`. ![Screenshot showing Quick Open in the Command Palette.](../images/getting-started/quick-open.png) * **Symbol search mode (`#`)**: replace the `>` symbol with `#` to search for symbols such as variables and functions. > [!TIP] > The Command Palette uses fuzzy matching. For example, typing `odks` finds the `Open Default Keyboard Shortcuts` command.
